# Job cards: numbering, status, invoicing, notes and assignees

> Detail split out of CLAUDE.md. Read before touching job numbering, job status, invoicing/archiving, deletion, comments or who is assigned.

## Numbering

**Job card auto-numbering**: Job numbers are auto-generated from two settings: `job_number_prefix` (e.g. `"DH-"`) and `job_number_next` (e.g. `"00001"`). The format preserves leading zeros (width of `job_number_next` string). On each job card creation, the server generates `{prefix}{paddedNumber}`, validates uniqueness, inserts the record, then increments `job_number_next`. Deleted job numbers are never reused (counter only goes forward). The job number field is read-only in the create form. Admin configures prefix and starting number in Settings > Job Card Numbering. If not configured, job card creation is blocked with an error message.

## Work-driven automatic status

**Work-driven automatic status**: A job's status follows the shop floor — it is recomputed from logged work on every work event (timer start/stop, time block added or deleted, finished quantity edited) by `syncStatusToWork` in `server/src/utils/jobStatusAuto.js`. Rule: every line at (or over) its ordered quantity ⇒ `DONE`; otherwise ⇒ `IN_PROGRESS`. Completion sums the good pieces (`qty`) from **finished** time blocks per line and compares to the line's quantity; a job with no lines, or any line whose quantity is missing/zero, is never complete. This **overrides** a manual status flip: if a manager moves a job elsewhere and a worker then logs work, it snaps back to match reality — to hold a finished job in another state the work itself must change. The only status it never touches is `INVOICED` (terminal); it also no-ops on archived jobs and when the status already matches. It does **not** write its own history row — it returns the `{ from, to }` change (or null) and the calling work route folds it into the history entry it already writes for that work event, so one action shows as one audit row carrying both the work change and the status move. Auto-status failures never break the work action. This is why **quantity is now required and must be a positive whole number** on every line item — it is the completion target. Enforced client-side (`jobCardValidation.mjs`, number input in `ItemsTab.jsx`) and server-side (`validateItemQuantities` in `validation.js`) on create and update.

## Invoicing and archiving

**Auto-archive on INVOICED**: When a job card's status transitions to `INVOICED` (via `PUT /:id` or `PATCH /:id/status`), the server automatically sets `archived = 1` and stamps `invoicedDate` with the current timestamp — on **both** routes the status write and the archive write run inside one `db.transaction`, so a failure between them can't leave a job reading INVOICED while still in the open list. Only management can set status to INVOICED. **Invoicing is an update-only transition**: a job is never *created* as INVOICED — the create route (`POST /`) rejects a `status` of `INVOICED` with 400, because only the update/status paths run the auto-archive + missing-files check, so allowing it at creation would strand a job in the invoiced-but-still-open limbo the status-lock exists to prevent. The status picker on the job screen mirrors this (INVOICED is offered only when editing an existing job, never while creating one). There is no manual archive endpoint; unarchive (`POST /:id/unarchive`, management) is the only way to reverse it. **An archived (invoiced/filed-away) job is status-locked**: both status-changing paths refuse any status change while `archived === 1` (returns 409 **before any write**) — `PATCH /:id/status` blocks every status change, and `PUT /:id` blocks a status change while still allowing edits to other fields — so even an admin can't recreate the filed-away-but-OPEN limbo by editing. The lock keys off the `archived` flag alone (invoicing always files a job away; unarchive always clears it). **Unarchive also resets `status` to `OPEN`** (in the same `unarchive` query) so a re-opened job returns as a normal working job rather than a back-in-the-list-but-still-INVOICED contradiction; the reset is recorded in history alongside the `archived`/`invoicedDate` changes.

**Soft close-out checkpoint**: When `PUT /jobcards/:id` or `PATCH /jobcards/:id/status` would set status to `INVOICED` (which also archives) and any attachment gaps exist, the server returns 409 `{ error: 'MISSING_ATTACHMENTS', attachmentWarnings }` **before any write**. The client shows an "Invoice anyway?" confirm and resends with `confirmMissingAttachments: true` in the body to bypass the check. This is a soft nudge, not a hard block.

## Deleting a job

**Soft delete checkpoint**: `DELETE /jobcards/:id` (admin) never deletes on the first request — because deleting is permanent and the job number is never reused, the server always returns 409 `{ error: 'CONFIRM_DELETE', workWarning }` **before any write** unless the body carries `confirmDelete: true`. `workWarning` is `null` when the job has no recorded work (client shows a plain "are you sure"); when any time has been logged or a timer is running (both cascade away on delete) it carries `{ hasActive, activeWorkers, loggedHours, pastWorkers }` so the confirm can name who/what is being erased. The confirmation lives entirely in this one 409 round-trip — there is no separate client-side pre-confirm — so the admin only ever sees a single dialog. Resending with `confirmDelete: true` bypasses the gate. Mirrors the missing-attachments checkpoint.

## Comments (notes)

Notes endpoints: `GET /jobcards/:id/notes` (authenticated — **newest first**, `created_at DESC` with `rowid` as tie-break), `POST /jobcards/:id/notes` (authenticated), `DELETE /jobcards/:id/notes/:noteId` (management). The **job list response also carries each job's newest comment** as `latestNote` (`{ text, userName, createdAt }`, or `null`) — fetched for all listed jobs in one pass by `getLatestNotesForJobcards` (`db/queries/operations.js`, a `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY jobcard_id ORDER BY created_at DESC, rowid DESC)` pick, i.e. **the same ordering the thread uses**, so the column can never show a different comment than the top of the thread when two share a timestamp; it returns raw rows and the route converts to camelCase at the boundary) and rendered as the **Latest Comment** column sitting between Status and Priority in the job list (full text floats on hover with author + time). Adding or deleting a comment in the job screen hands the newest remaining comment back to the list via `onNotesChange`, which **patches that one row in place** (never a whole-list re-fetch). The column id `latestNote` must exist in **both** `DEFAULT_COLUMN_ORDER` (`JobCardList.constants.js`) and its server mirror `JOBCARD_COLUMN_IDS` (`middleware/validation.js`) — the server validates saved column order/visibility against that list, so a column missing there breaks reordering for everyone. `mergeColumnOrder` folds a newly-added column into a user's saved order at its default position and always keeps `actions` last. The Excel export re-reverses the thread so its Notes cell still reads oldest-first.

## Assignees

Assignee endpoints: the full assignee list is replaced through `PUT /jobcards/:id` (management) — there is no separate assignee-replace route; `POST /jobcards/:id/assignees/self` (authenticated, idempotent self-assign — uses `req.user.userId`, body ignored), `DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/self` (authenticated, idempotent self-unassign). Self routes log history with action `self_assign` / `self_unassign`.
